adam-gilmore.name: Adam Gilmore
adam-gilmore.bio: Adam Gilmore is an English game musician and programmer whose computer-game work began while he was still a teenager. He became associated with Zeppelin Games and wrote music across 8-bit and 16-bit formats, including Commodore 64 and Amiga releases, before moving away from game music in the mid-1990s.

al-lowe.name: Al Lowe
al-lowe.bio: Al Lowe is an American game designer, programmer and musician best known for his long career at Sierra On-Line and for creating Leisure Suit Larry. Before that series, he worked on educational and entertainment software including Donald Duck’s Playground, represented in the CCG C64 archive, and frequently combined programming, design and music duties.

sources.title: The Sierra Chest - Al Lowe biography

alan-mckean.name: Alan McKean
alan-mckean.bio: Alan McKean is a game composer and audio director whose credits span the late-1980s and 1990s, including a substantial run of work with Dynamix. His C64 credits in the CCG archive are Caveman Ugh-Lympics and Project Firestart, followed by audio work on titles such as A-10 Tank Killer, Red Baron and The Adventures of Willy Beamish.

allister-brimble.name: Allister Brimble
allister-brimble.bio: Allister Brimble is a British game composer and sound designer whose career spans the home-computer era through to modern games. His Amiga work includes music and audio for titles such as Alien Breed, Project-X, Superfrog and Zeewolf, while his wider career covers hundreds of game soundtracks across numerous platforms.

andrew-barnabas.name: Andrew Barnabas
andrew-barnabas.bio: Andrew Barnabas is a British Guyanese composer whose career began with tracker music and game audio before expanding into film and television. His early game work includes Amiga arrangements and original scores, while later credits include MediEvil and a long-running composing partnership through Bob & Barn and AB Music.

antony-crowther.name: Antony Crowther
antony-crowther.bio: Antony Crowther is a British programmer, designer and musician who became active during the early UK home-computer boom. He developed and published games through the 1980s, worked with Alligata, and collaborated musically with his school friend Ben Daglish; his credits span programming, design, graphics and sound rather than music alone.

archer-maclean.name: Archer MacLean
archer-maclean.bio: Archer MacLean was a British programmer, designer and game creator best known for Dropzone, International Karate, IK+ and his later snooker and pool games. He was primarily a designer and programmer rather than a career composer, but his multi-discipline credits include sound work represented in the CCG Amiga archive.

barry-leitch.name: Barry Leitch
barry-leitch.bio: Barry Leitch is a Scottish video-game composer whose professional career began in his teens. After early C64 work he joined Imagitec and went on to contribute music and sound to a large range of home-computer and console games, including Lotus Turbo Challenge 2, HeroQuest and Super Cars II in the CCG archive.

sources.title: Video Game Music Preservation Foundation profile

ben-daglish.name: Ben Daglish
ben-daglish.bio: Ben Daglish (1966–2018) was an English composer and multi-instrumentalist whose music became closely associated with British home-computer games. He grew up in Sheffield, where he met programmer Tony Crowther at school. They later formed the W.E.M.U.S.I.C. partnership, with Crowther developing music playback software and Daglish composing and entering the notes for the Commodore 64. His game scores included Loco, Trap, Deflektor, Krakout and The Last Ninja, the latter sharing music duties with Anthony Lees. Trap became especially memorable for its lengthy title music and the hidden Gladiator animation. In interviews, Daglish singled out Trap as a personal favourite, while acknowledging the popularity of his Last Ninja melodies. Away from games, he continued performing and composing for theatre and live events. He played a wide range of instruments and remained involved with retro-gaming concerts and the C64 music community.

bjorn-lynne.name: Bjørn Lynne
bjorn-lynne.bio: Bjørn Lynne is a Norwegian composer who first became widely known in the Amiga demoscene under the handle Dr. Awesome. He later moved into commercial game music, including work connected with Team17 and the Worms series, while maintaining a long independent recording career.

bob-vieira.name: Bob Vieira
bob-vieira.bio: Bob Vieira is a game-audio contributor associated with Epyx-era Commodore 64 releases. The CCG archive links him to The Movie Monster Game, Summer Games II and Super Cycle, placing his recorded work within the mid-1980s American C64 publishing scene.

brian-doe.name: Brian Doe
brian-doe.bio: Brian Doe is credited with Commodore 64 music on early British releases including Cliff Hanger and Trashman. Public biographical information is limited, so this profile concentrates on the verified game credits rather than adding unsupported personal details.
